title: Variance investigation: clock drift, thermal throttling, and cluster/driver mismatch in FP8/INT8 benchmarks
creator: Talia Benson
description:
Context
We observed high run-to-run variance in benchmark results during FP8/INT8 sprint calibration, especially on H100 in mixed prefill/decode workloads (TTFT and TPOT shifting enough to flip “win/loss” vs baseline). This ticket documents the investigation, root causes, and mitigations applied to the harness + fleet runner so the matrix results are defensible and can be used to drive kernel auto-selection and scheduler tuning.

Impact / why P0
- Variance was large enough to invalidate kernel comparisons and could lead to shipping the wrong auto-select heuristics.
- Noisy signals would also make perf-canary thresholds too twitchy (false positives) during rollout.

Observed symptoms (from calibration + early matrix runs)
- TTFT p50 stable-ish, but TTFT p95 and TPOT showed multi-run spread of ~8–20% for the same case (same model/shape/config).
- A subset of runs had “sawtooth” tokens/s where decode slowed over time.
- H100 results differed meaningfully across clusters/regions even with same git SHA and benchmark config.

Hypotheses evaluated
1) GPU clocks not pinned → drift between runs; boosting behavior differed by thermal/power headroom.
2) Thermal throttling / power limit → long-running runs or concurrent jobs reduce effective clocks.
3) Shared-node contention (MPS, other pods, noisy neighbors) → intermittent slowdowns.
4) Driver/CUDA mismatch across clusters → kernel selection differences and perf deltas.
5) Harness-level measurement artifacts (warmup too short, debug logging, async timing) → spurious variance.

What we measured / how
We standardized a “variance triage checklist” for any suspicious benchmark case:
- Capture per-run metadata: git SHA, container tag, CUDA version, NVIDIA driver, GPU UUID, MIG mode, persistence mode.
- Record clocks + thermals: SM clock, mem clock, temperature, power draw, power limit at start/mid/end.
- Confirm node exclusivity: ensure no other workload on GPU (best-effort via runner scheduling + manual spot checks).
- Repeat runs (N=10) with identical config; compute p50/p95 and coefficient of variation (CV) for TTFT/TPOT/tokens/s.

Findings / root causes
A) Clock drift was real and large enough to flip outcomes
- On H100, default clock behavior varied materially across nodes; we saw SM clock ranges spanning ~200–400MHz across runs depending on thermal headroom.
- In multi-minute cases, clocks could decay over time (thermal/power) → sawtooth tokens/s.

B) Thermal throttling and power management contributed to long-tail variance
- Runs on “warm” nodes (prior heavy use) showed higher starting temps and earlier throttle.
- Some nodes had slightly different power-limit settings; even small differences shifted decode throughput.

C) Driver/CUDA mismatches across clusters
- Not all clusters were on the same driver minor; a subset ran an older driver that changed kernel perf characteristics (and in one case, impacted FP8 path selection).
- This explains “region A faster than region B” for identical configs.

D) Shared-node contention (secondary factor)
- A handful of outlier runs correlated with other activity on the same host / GPU. This was rarer once we reserved dedicated pools, but still happened in early unreserved windows.

E) Harness measurement artifacts (confirmed, fixed)
- Debug logging in a hot loop materially perturbed timing for small batch/short decode benchmarks (created fake regressions, increased jitter).
- Warmup count was insufficient for some cases; first measured iteration included cache/warmup behavior.

Mitigations shipped / applied
1) Pin driver/CUDA container + optional clock locking in benchmark-lab runner
- Implemented via benchmark-lab PR-851:
  - enforce runner image pinning per matrix run
  - validate driver/CUDA compatibility upfront
  - add optional GPU clock locking (documented as default-on for official matrix runs)
- Operational note: clocks are locked only for benchmark pools; not applied to customer-serving nodes.

2) Add structured artifact metadata for reproducibility
- Implemented via redwood PR-19880:
  - every run exports metadata (git SHA, container digest, driver/CUDA versions, clock settings, GPU UUID, node ID, model hash, benchmark config)
  - this unblocked post-hoc clustering of results by environment and fast identification of “bad runs”

3) Remove/gate debug logging that perturbed benchmarks
- Implemented via redwood PR-19918:
  - moved debug logs behind an off-by-default flag
  - verified that disabling logs reduced jitter in short benchmarks

4) Fleet/infra guardrails (coordination with Infra/SRE)
- Use reserved benchmark pools where possible; avoid shared nodes.
- Added a preflight check in runbook: fail fast if driver is not in the approved list for the sprint.
- Documented “cooldown” guidance between long runs on the same node (or rotate nodes) when clock locking is not possible.

Updated benchmark standards (operational)
- Official matrix runs require:
  - pinned container image + recorded driver/CUDA
  - clock locking enabled (where permitted)
  - minimum N=5 runs for end-to-end; N=10 for cases used in decision-making (heuristics)
  - report variance (CV or p95/p50 spread) alongside p50/p95
  - exclude outliers only with documented cause (contention/driver mismatch) and keep raw artifacts

Results after mitigations (summary)
- H100 end-to-end mixed workload cases: run-to-run CV reduced from ~6–12% to ~1–3% for tokens/s; TTFT p95 spread reduced materially.
- A100 was less sensitive but still benefited from pinned environment and warmups.
- Remaining variance now mostly tracks request-level randomness (scheduler interleaving effects) rather than machine/environment drift.

Decision / guidance for the sprint
- Kernel win claims must be backed by “post-mitigation” runs only.
- Any case showing >5% CV after mitigations must be escalated to (a) contention investigation or (b) profiling (nsys) before it can drive heuristics.

Follow-ups
- Close-the-loop with perf-canary thresholds: now that benchmark noise is lower, thresholds can be tighter without false positives.
- Add an automated “environment conformance” check to matrix runner (hard fail on unapproved driver/CUDA) as a separate hardening task.

- Runner fix: sources/github/benchmark-lab/pr-851-pin-driver-cuda-and-gpu-clocks-in-runner.json

comments: 2026-02-10 (Talia Benson): Marking P0. We can’t sign off methodology or publish the matrix if we can’t reproduce within a few % on the same config. Assigning to Rina as harness owner; looping in Irene (fleet) + Claire (methodology).

2026-02-11 (Rina Kobayashi): Repro: H100, same model+workload, 10 runs show ~12% spread tokens/s; TTFT p95 swings. Not seeing same magnitude on A100. Suspect clocks/thermals + cluster mismatch. Starting with clock/thermal telemetry capture and comparing two clusters.

2026-02-12 (Irene Choi): Confirmed: two clusters not on the same driver minor; we’ll align benchmark pools and/or route jobs only to approved driver during the sprint. Also seeing some nodes with different power cap defaults; investigating.

2026-02-14 (Rina Kobayashi): Found debug logging in measurement loop (small batch cases). Disabling drops jitter immediately. Filing PR to gate logs. Still seeing drift on long runs → likely thermals/clocks.

2026-02-16 (Rina Kobayashi): With locked clocks + pinned container (runner WIP), H100 CV down to ~2% on the worst offenders. Shared-node contention produced a couple big outliers; recommending dedicated benchmark pools + preflight checks.

2026-02-18 (Claire Dubois): Please ensure benchmark matrix reports variance explicitly and includes environment metadata. Also: define rules for excluding outliers; we should keep raw artifacts even if we exclude from aggregates.

2026-02-22 (Talia Benson): Closing as Done. Mitigations landed (runner pinning + clock lock option, artifact metadata, debug logging fix) and runbook updated. Next: ensure matrix runner hard-fails on driver mismatch and update perf-canary noise assumptions.
